reason: Survey of graph-based agent memory: taxonomy, life-cycle techniques, libraries and open directions; secondary study, no primary method.
LightMem is a memory system for agents; reported claims are LoCoMo F1 (+2.5 over A-MEM) and latency, i.e. retrieval and task outcomes, not loop control.
RoMeRL is a learned memory-utility system; claims are ALFWorld/LifelongAgentBench task performance and memory-store efficiency, not how the loop proceeds.
SF-AMS forgetting/importance scoring evaluated by LoCoMo and LongMemEval-s F1 gains over LightMem, MemO, A-Mem: retrieval quality, not loop control.
AMA is a multi-agent memory system; its Judge triggers re-retrieval, but reported claims are long-context benchmark gains and ~80% token savings.
Position/overview paper: taxonomizes the multi-agent security threat landscape and proposes a research agenda; no primary contribution.
Feedback-to-memory continual learning; claims are tau-bench single-trial success (1.6x, 2.6x baseline) and cross-model transfer, i.e. task outcomes.
Budget-based metabolism makes persistence normative and asynchronous processes drive runs; reports a shift from reactive to spontaneous activity (triggering/scheduling).
Reference architecture for retail agent networks with orchestration and guardrails; claims are deployment patterns, reliability/cost SLOs in three case studies.
TANGLE is a 541-instance benchmark for memory conflict handling (perception, calibration, clarification, faithfulness); measures no loop-control property.
Measures agent-harness self-evolution updates, comparing ACE, TF-GRPO and AHE: frequent updates fail on held-out data, snapshots collapse (iteration policy of the update loop).
SoK: taxonomy, architectural decomposition and research roadmap for agentic RAG; secondary study, retained as a snowballing seed.
Survey of agentic-AI evaluation with an eleven-dimensional taxonomy of metrics, benchmarks and gaps; secondary study.
MemEvoBench is a safety benchmark of memory misevolution across 7 domains and 36 risk types; measures behavioural safety degradation, not a loop-control property.
ZifaMem structured memory judged by emotional-intelligence scores, persona grounding and preference endpoints: output quality, not loop control.
PersonaVLM is a personalized multimodal agent plus Persona-MME benchmark; claims are 22.4%/9.8% benchmark gains over baselines and GPT-4o.
Survey of trajectory data management and mining from deep learning to LLMs, with datasets and toolkits; secondary study and no agent loop.
MemGUI-Agent's Context-as-Action is trained via MemGUI-3K, but reported claims are MemGUI-Bench and MobileWorld GUI task performance.
Surfaces recency and remaining budget so the agent makes keep-or-archive decisions; ablations show the dashboard matters beyond archive/recovery tools (loop state).
Integrates a memoryless risk encoder over time into an escalation signal; stateless agents show sharp cliffs, second-order dynamics smooth ones (loop state driving escalation).
TokenPilot compaction and eviction framework; claims are 56-87% cost reduction with competitive task performance, i.e. system outcomes, not loop control.
Hands-on tutorial introducing multi-turn RL fine-tuning for LLM agents on Amazon SageMaker AI; not a research contribution.
Tree Training is a training pipeline for tree-structured trajectories (DFS serialization, partitioning); the claim is up to 6.2x training speedup.
PACEvolve's backtracking and sampling policy govern an evolutionary search, but reported claims are SOTA on LLM-SR and KernelBench and a Modded NanoGPT record.
ERA is a two-stage prior-learning plus online RL framework; claims are EB-ALFRED +8.4% and EB-Manipulation +19.4% over GPT-4o.
Lean4 verification of agent workflows plus LeanEvolve repair; verification-passing workflows beat failing ones by 11.94%, a claim about the verifier (verification, repair).
MiniMax-M2 model series report: data pipelines, an RL system and checkpoints, claimed by frontier-tier performance on agentic coding, search and reasoning benchmarks.
Agent World Model is a synthetic environment pipeline for agentic RL; claims are out-of-distribution generalization across three benchmarks.
DPEPO adds parallel exploration plus SFT/RL with diversity rewards, but reported claims are SOTA success rates on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld.
Review of the LLM landscape and theoretical explanations for generalization capacity; secondary study with no agent loop.
25,000 runs: scaffold explains 1.5% of variance vs 41.4% for the base model, evidence ignored in 68% of traces, belief revision in 26% (negative result on self-correction).
RTPO is a multi-turn RL training algorithm (reverse trees, turn-level credit); reported claims are 21.50% and 10.76% gains over trajectory- and turn-level baselines.
OpenSeeker-v2 is an SFT data recipe for search agents; claims are BrowseComp, HLE and xbench scores against Tongyi DeepResearch.
SWE-World replaces containers with a learned surrogate for training and test-time selection; claims are SWE-bench Verified scores from 6.2% to 68.2%.
M2 dual-tier memory for web agents; claims are up to 19.6% success-rate gain and 58.7% token reduction on WebVoyager and OnlineMind2Web.
Kosmos is an AI-scientist system; reported claims are 79.4% statement accuracy, seven discoveries and researcher-time equivalence, not evidence about its cycle control.
Identifies premature termination, shows its rate rises with context length at fixed difficulty, and analyses seven context-management methods that lower it (termination).
ARC compaction is evaluated by Needle-in-a-Haystack exact-answer accuracy (99.40% vs 88.12%), LongBench-v2 accuracy and serving cost: retrieval quality, not loop control.
PerspectiveGap is a 110-scenario benchmark scoring 33 models on writing orchestration prompts (pass and leakage rates); model capability, not a loop property.
CompanionCast orchestrates companion agents for shared sports viewing; pilot claims are perceived social presence and emotional sharing versus solitary viewing.
Secondary study over an 84-entry curated pool with an exclusion log, mapping RL reward, credit and orchestration axes; retained as a snowballing seed.
Overview of a deep and multi-agent RL research portfolio (policy coordination, communication, intrinsic motivation); no language-model agent loop.
Models collaboration as a temporal graph to detect and mitigate hallucination and error propagation, with accuracy reported for the detector (verification of intermediate results).
Learns the orchestration spec with counterfactual rewards on edited role, capacity and dependency spans, versus other orchestration methods (control topology as studied variable).
DiMo is a four-agent debate framework; claims are accuracy gains over single-model and debate baselines on six benchmarks plus interpretability.
